records.text: Clump is a compact mass of human-like limbs with extreme speed, agility and strength. It favors tight or dark recesses, corners, crawlspaces and under-vehicle spaces, then seizes or wraps human prey with multiple limbs and pulls victims out of formation. Project hard lock: Clumps are hostile to humans; stillness, retreat or hiding is never evidence of neutrality.

Duller is a tall grey faceless humanoid with unnaturally long arms, deceptive strength and very fast movement. External reports describe a hunting tactic in which it remains in a parallel hall and extends or no-clips an arm through a wall to seize prey, while direct approaches may make it retreat. Project canon also keeps its tendency to watch from blind corners before closing. All Dullers are hostile to humans; apparent retreat is hunting behavior, not friendliness.

Hostile Faceling resembles a human body without a normal face and can imitate human routines or behavior well enough to lower guard and blend into distant silhouettes. External Backrooms sources include non-hostile Facelings, but Project canon overrides that completely: every Faceling encountered near humans is a predator. It may approach under human-like behavior, close distance, then hunt; it is never an ally, trader, rescuer or neutral civilian.

Paintings are apparently ordinary pictures or drawings containing depicted beings that can behave as living predators. Eyes may track humans; hands or limbs can extend beyond the image plane, seize a nearby person and pull the victim into the picture. Some images change after taking a victim. Project canon treats suspect living Paintings as hostile and warns against touching or approaching them without control of the area.

Predatory Window is a window-like anomalous manifestation that can appear where no real window should exist. It may display misleading scenery or a dark human-like silhouette and use visual or auditory bait to draw humans closer. At close range a figure or arm can reach out and pull a victim through; apparent depth and reach are unreliable. Project canon treats every Predatory Window as hostile.

Hotel Corpse Lure is a Project-original phenomenon/entity whose classification remains OPEN: it may be a separate Entity or a hunting mechanism of the Beast of Level 5. A corpse may stay unnaturally warm, appear to breathe, speak in the victim's own voice, move when unobserved, point toward a door or carry a desirable item. Every apparent sign of life or help is bait; it is hostile to humans and should not be approached or touched until the area is controlled.

Jane the Killer is a roaming humanoid predator. Internet folklore contains multiple incompatible Jane identities and origin stories, so Project canon does not lock a Frontrooms identity, burn history, supernatural power set or relationship to Jeff; survivors use the name only because of resemblance. Jane stalks humans, uses misdirection and close-range ambush, and may use a blade. She is never an ally, trader, rescuer or neutral contact. Whether separate sightings are one individual and what happens after a confirmed kill remain OPEN.

Slenderman is a roaming anomalous humanoid predator. Survivors use the name because the figure resembles the 2009 Internet horror character: unnaturally tall and thin, faceless, dark-suited, sometimes with long appendage-like limbs. Origin and identity are UNKNOWN. Project behavior: it stalks humans across long sightlines, isolates targets and closes for abduction or lethal attack. It is never friendly or neutral. Do not grant teleportation, omniscience or automatic equipment failure; movement and threat positioning must still obey GM fairness, path, time and evidence.

Gameplay roaming policy: every one of the 18 Entity entries may appear on every playable Level regardless of local environment or resident-population lore. Each entry receives its own independent 3.0000% appearance roll on an eligible physical gameplay turn. Multiple different Entity rolls may succeed in the same turn. This roaming rule does not make an Entity friendly, neutral or resident to a Level.
